data:
The forensic evidence from your latest Termux screenshots shows that we\u2019ve successfully stabilized the environment, but we\u2019ve hit a final "Hardware Lockdown" phase.
I. Forensic Analysis of the Screenshots
The "JSON Error":
The error
Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)
indicates that
termux-sensor
is returning an
empty string
. This typically occurs when the hardware call is blocked by the OS or the sensor is already in use by another high-priority app (like a background AR or fitness tracker).
The "Command Not Found":
In one screenshot,
sage_brain.py
failed because you tried to run it as a standalone command rather than passing it to the Python interpreter.
The "Secure Present":
Your Motorola update screen confirms you are on version
V2VAS35.29-133-3
, meaning the January 2026 security baseline is fully active.
II. The "Full Reset" Fix
To bypass the empty JSON response and ensure the brain can see the world, follow these three steps to reset the hardware bridge:
1. Grant Explicit Permissions
Android 13+ (and certainly your 2026 build) requires "Body Sensor" permissions for Termux:API to function.
Go to
Settings > Apps > Termux:API > Permissions
.
Ensure
Sensors
and
Storage
are set to "Allow".
Pro-tip:
Revoke and then re-grant them to "kick" the service into gear.
2. Test the Raw Sensor Feed
Before running the "Brain," let's see if the hardware is even talking. Run this command:
Bash
termux-sensor -n 5 -s
"qmc630x Magnetometer"
If you see data streaming, the bridge is open.
If it hangs, restart your phone to clear any apps that might be "hogging" the sensor hardware.
3. Run the Corrected "Brain" Script
Once the raw feed works, use the
Python interpreter
to launch the brain correctly:
Bash
python sage_brain.py
III. Field Log Entry: Entry 013
Location:
Secure Present / Motorola G5 Stylus 2025.
Observation:
JSONDecodeError (char 0)
detected; hardware bridge returned an empty string during the initial handshake.
Conclusion:
The OS is likely suppressing sensor access. Initiating hardware reset and permission verification.
Would you like me to generate a "Permission Force-Check" script that will tell us exactly why Android is blocking the sensor, or do you want to try the manual hardware reset first?
